standard: PCAF (2025). Global GHG Accounting and Reporting Standard Part A: Financed Emissions. Third Edition, §5.6 (pp.90–96).
note: The vehicle-type statistics the §5.6 engine reaches for when a vehicle's make and model efficiency or its distance is not known (Options 3a and 3b), and the energy content that turns a litre of fuel into the kWh the fuel-factor baseline is held per. Every efficiency figure is PROVISIONAL and says so: an order-of-magnitude class average from published model figures and global ranges, not a Sri Lankan measurement and not a licensed dataset — docs/BASELINE-REGISTER.md §3.5.3 records that no Sri Lankan class-average figure has been verified. The annual distances are the registry's (vehicle_annual_distance_km, ESMAP 2000, disclosed as such); the ones held here are the fallback where the registry holds nothing for the class. A run that uses this set carries its version and checksum, and the report repeats the provisional mark.

energyContent.unit: kWh per litre (net calorific value × density)

petrol.source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines Vol. 2 Table 1.2 (motor gasoline NCV 44.3 TJ/Gg) with a density of 0.74 kg/L: 32.8 MJ/L = 9.1 kWh/L; DEFRA 2024 uses 32.2 MJ/L — 8.94 kWh/L is the DEFRA figure, the lower of the two

diesel.source: IPCC 2006 Vol. 2 Table 1.2 (gas/diesel oil NCV 43.0 TJ/Gg) with a density of 0.84 kg/L: 36.1 MJ/L = 10.0 kWh/L; DEFRA 2024 35.9 MJ/L = 9.97 kWh/L

efficiency.source: Order-of-magnitude for the Sri Lankan petrol car park (Toyota Aqua 33.6 km/L WLTC at the efficient end, a 1.5 L saloon at 7–8 L/100 km); not a measured class average

annualDistance_km.source: World Bank/ESMAP ESM262 (2000 fleet), secondary_reported — the registry's vehicle_annual_distance_km carries the same figure

efficiency.source: Order-of-magnitude for diesel cars and SUVs; not a measured class average
Honda Vezel HEV 27.0 km/L JC08 (2013) and Toyota Aqua 33.6 km/L WLTC bracket 3–4 L/100 km; JC08 overstates real-world by roughly a quarter
Nissan Leaf 40 kWh 14.0 and BYD Atto 3 13.8 kWh/100 km WLTP (docs/BASELINE-REGISTER.md §3.5.3)
Order-of-magnitude for 100–150 cc commuter motorcycles (45 km/L); not a measured class average
Order-of-magnitude for electric scooters (2–3 kWh/100 km); not a measured class average
Order-of-magnitude for light commercial vans; not a measured class average

annualDistance_km.source: As diesel cars, ESMAP ESM262 (2000) — vans and lorries were not verified (docs/BASELINE-REGISTER.md §3.5.2)

efficiency.source: Order-of-magnitude for medium rigid trucks; not a measured class average

annualDistance_km.source: Indicative; not verified for Sri Lanka

efficiency.source: Order-of-magnitude for diesel buses; not a measured class average

annualDistance_km.source: SLTB operated km ÷ average fleet, NTC 2019 via mirror, derived (docs/BASELINE-REGISTER.md §3.5.2)

efficiency.source: Option 3b only: the petrol-car figure, because a car is the likeliest financed vehicle where nothing else is known; a run on this row scores 5 and says so
